payload.description:
ASP301 (raise+return) and ASP302 (Optional/None annotation) both key on the NONE sentinel; neither catches the EMPTY-COLLECTION sentinel: returning an empty/falsy literal from an except/error branch when the return type is a bare collection. That conflates 'read failed (unknown)' with 'read succeeded, zero records' — and is worse than the None case ASP302 covers, because [] is a legitimate success value. Live instance: gateway laconic_registry._fetch_records_raw returns -> list[dict] and `return []` inside `except httpx.HTTPError` and on a GraphQL-errors branch; this made a wallet's 8 on-chain boxes render as 0 on a transient read error.

Add ASP303 (level3, sibling to ASP301/302): report a `return` of an empty/falsy literal ([], {}, set(), '', 0, None, False) lexically inside an `except` clause, in a function whose return annotation is NOT Result/Optional -> 'error swallowed into a success-shaped sentinel; return Result'. High precision: returning a nothing-literal from an except handler is almost always error-swallowing. First INVALID fixture = the _fetch_records_raw shape (`except X: return []`). VALID: a genuine `return []` NOT inside an except; a function returning Result[...]; an except that re-raises.

Acceptance (refactor; rule fixtures are the assertion): rule fires on INVALID (incl. except->[] / except->{} / except->'' shapes), clean on VALID; aspergillus python tests pass (pytest python/tests). MTM consumes at error+autofix-or-absent (past warn phase). Subtree aspergillus/.
payload.title: ASP303: flag error->empty/falsy-literal sentinel (return [] in an except) — the gap ASP301/302 miss

payload.description:
Add an aspergillus rule (Python: fixit/LibCST; the TS analogue is an ast-grep/ESLint rule) that detects and forbids the STRINGLY-TYPED OPTIONAL antipattern — encoding 'maybe absent' as an empty string instead of `T | None`. This is the static-detection layer that makes the gw-baf class of bug UNCONSTRUCTABLE at commit time, regardless of any coordinator/worker diligence (per the principal: 'if the coordinator CAN make the error, it is a tooling gap').

## Motivating crash (the fixture)
gw-baf: the prod gateway crash-looped at startup because `gateway_wallet_private_key: str = ''` let `if not private_key: return` (treats '' as absent) coexist with `Keypair.from_base58_string(private_key)` (assumes present). Both sides are `str`, so mypy could not see the contradiction; the bug only surfaced when the prod (Privy, no-raw-key) config booted on-chain. The empty-string-as-absent sentinel is the enabling pattern.

## What the rule detects (syntactic, no execution, no dataflow needed)
Flag, in config/Settings construction:
- `os.environ.get(NAME, "")` used as a field default (the inline sentinel).
- `field(default="")` / `default_factory` returning `""` for a secret/identity/config field.
- helper functions that return `""` for 'unset' (e.g. mtm-gateway's `_secret_from_file_or_env` final `return os.environ.get(value_env, "")`).
Require instead `T | None` (default `None`) — OR a tagged-union/Result variant. The fix at the SOURCE (the default site) is purely local/AST-visible; the type system then does the cross-function propagation for free: once the field is `str | None`, every consumer must handle `None`, so `from_base58_string(None)` won't typecheck. AST rule kills the source; mypy --strict kills every unguarded use.

## Why this is the right layer
- Generalizes beyond the treasury key: it retires the whole empty-string-sentinel convention (config.py `_secret_from_file_or_env`, the `os.environ.get(x, '')` defaults) — the recurring enabler.
- Static + pre-commit-gated: MTM already gates every commit on aspergillus, so the sentinel can't re-enter. No reliance on remembering an audit or booting an artifact.
- Correct-by-construction: the invalid state stops being representable.

## Scope / engine
- Python rule via fixit/LibCST (matches the gateway/backtest corpus). Provide an AUTOFIX where mechanical (`get(x, "")` -> `get(x)` returning `str | None`; sentinel `return ""` -> `return None` with signature change).
- Follow the severity-graduation workflow (aspergillus/docs/decisions/2026-05-19-severity-graduation.md): land at warn, fix the existing corpus (mtm gateway config sentinels), then promote to error+autofix per MTM's past-warn policy (docs/decisions/2026-05-19-mtm-past-warn-promotion-phase.md).
- Heuristic scoping: target Settings/config dataclasses + os.environ.get-with-empty-default + *_FILE/secret helpers; avoid false positives on genuine empty-string domain defaults (e.g. an optional display label) — gate on name/annotation signals (key/secret/private/token/id/address/url) or on the value flowing to a parser/constructor. Document the scoping in the rule.

## Acceptance
- The rule FIRES on a fixture reproducing `gateway_wallet_private_key: str = ''` + `_secret_from_file_or_env` returning '' (RED), and PASSES once they are `T | None` (GREEN).
- Applied to the mtm gateway, it flags the existing sentinels gw-baf must remove (cross-check: the two land together).
- Autofix (where provided) produces type-correct `T | None` and the gateway still mypy --strict passes after the consumers handle None.
- Wired into the aspergillus rule corpus + MTM pre-commit per severity-graduation.

Cross-ref: gw-baf (the crash + the corpus fix this rule enforces), dep-955 / gw-f34 (the Privy backend whose 'no raw key' world the sentinel hid), aspergillus/docs/design.md (multi-engine), severity-graduation ADR. Origin: 2026-06-11 prod-deploy RCA.
payload.title: Rule: ban empty-string sentinels for optional config/secret fields — require T | None so the type checker forces presence handling

payload.description:
KEYSTONE of the aspergillus-L3-everywhere epic (mtm root). The Python ASP202 rule (python/src/aspergillus/rules/level2.py) counts ONLY literal `assert` statements, so it false-positives on idiomatic Python and got blanket-DISABLED in both gateway (168 findings, ~100% pydantic validators) and backtest. The TS sibling (typescript/rules/asp202-min-assertions.js) already solved this with options (methodNames, countThrowStatements). Bring the Python rule to parity:

- Count `raise` statements as assertions (NASA: assert(cond) ≡ if !cond: raise). This alone covers raise-based guards.
- Recognize pydantic validation as assertion-equivalent: @field_validator / @model_validator methods, .model_validate()/.parse() calls, and (decide) Field(...)-constrained models — so a validator-bearing model method isn't flagged for lacking literal asserts.
- Make these CONFIGURABLE (parity with the TS methodNames/countThrowStatements), so a consumer can tune what counts without disabling the rule.

Acceptance: unit tests (the rule's own Valid/Invalid fixtures) for raise-counting + pydantic-validator recognition + the config knobs; run the enhanced rule against the gateway + backtest trees and show the false-positive count collapses (the 168 gateway findings drop to genuine low-assertion functions only). Round-trips to aspergillus upstream. Unblocks gw-/bt- re-enable. Points: 5

payload.description:
Follow-on to asp-070 (which made ASP202 recognize raise/validators/Field — done). asp-070's evidence: after recognition, the gateway residual is 261 GENUINE findings, 259/261 PURE functions (loaders/formatters/mappers/glue) with <2 preconditions. That is the RULE mis-prescribing, not under-asserted code: a pure function earns correctness from total functions + exhaustive types + property tests; runtime assertion density (NASA Rule #5 / ASP202) is the IMPERATIVE-SHELL mechanism — for functions that actually have runtime preconditions to check.

Per the universal-rigor doctrine (docs/engineering-practices.md § 'Why universal rigor'): the standard is NEVER lowered — full rigor everywhere — but the right MECHANISM per code shape. So refine ASP202 (both engines: python/src/aspergillus/rules/level2.py AND typescript/rules/asp202-min-assertions.js) to apply the assertion-density requirement where it is the correct mechanism — the imperative shell / functions with side effects or boundary preconditions (compose with the existing FC/IS signal: ASP205/206 io_blocklist / eslint-plugin-boundaries layers) — so pure-core functions are not mis-flagged (their correctness is enforced by the OTHER L3 rules: types, Result-not-throw, purity). Design the detection (the worker decides the precise predicate, grounded in the FC/IS boundary).

Acceptance: aspergillus tests green incl. new FC/IS Valid/Invalid fixtures (pure transform exempt; imperative-shell function with unchecked preconditions flagged); re-run over gateway+backtest+arcade — the residual collapses to the genuine imperative-shell low-assertion set (the small real number), demonstrated with before/after counts. payload.description: Surfaced during the mtm consumer re-enables (epic mtm-1d9). The TS asp202-min-assertions defaults to treatAwaitAsIo:true — bare 'await' counted as I/O. Evidence this is an over-approximation: async-everywhere React Native flags 92 functions under true (86 of them pure async orchestrators with NO real I/O and NO untrusted input — theatre-assert sites), vs 6 under treatAwaitAsIo:false, which matches gateway=6/backtest=8 and the Python rule. The Python LowAssertionDensity keys imperative-shell detection on REAL I/O (io_blocklist) + untrusted params, NOT 'is async' — 'await' is 'calls an async fn,' not I/O; the I/O lives at the actual I/O call site (which is itself flagged), so treatAwaitAsIo:false correctly attributes I/O to the call site, not every async caller. Both mtm TS consumers (arcade, mobile) are now configured treatAwaitAsIo:false for Python-parity. QUESTION for the corpus: should false be the DEFAULT (so TS matches its Python sibling + no consumer re-specifies the correct semantics)? This changes behavior for any non-mtm aspergillus consumer, hence a considered corpus decision, not a unilateral flip in the consumer flow. If yes, also re-confirm the asp-da5 arcade baseline under the corrected default. Round-trips to aspergillus upstream. Points: 2

payload.description: Surfaced during hilo-5e0 (arcade ASP202 wire, epic mtm-1d9). The TS asp202-min-assertions I/O detection counts window.matchMedia as an I/O boundary, so a presentational canvas-animation useEffect (HeroCandleChart, components/layout) — whose only matchMedia use is a reduced-motion capability query with correct graceful null-ref no-ops and ZERO assertable preconditions — is flagged as imperative shell needing assertions. matchMedia is a pure capability/feature query, not precondition-bearing I/O. Fix: drop window.matchMedia (and similar pure capability queries — matchMedia, devicePixelRatio readonly reads, etc.) from the TS I/O signal so it doesn't demand assertions on presentational effects. Add a fixture (a matchMedia-only effect is functional-core/exempt). Interim: hilo-5e0 carries a narrow justified eslint-disable citing this pebble. Round-trips to aspergillus upstream. Points: 2

payload.description:
IO_METHOD_NAMES (python/src/aspergillus/io_blocklist.py) lists 'rename' as a bare method name 'unambiguously I/O on any object'. It is NOT: pandas DataFrame.rename / Series.rename are pure in-memory ops. Any function doing df.rename(columns=...) or series.rename('x') is wrongly flagged ASP205 (ImpureFunction) and ASP206 (MixedIOAndLogic), and — post asp-da5 — wrongly classified as imperative-shell for ASP202 scoping.

Evidence (backtest subtree, surfaced by bt-4b5 re-enabling ASP202):
  - data_fetcher.py:_normalize_dune_df  -> df.rename(columns=...)  (pure)
  - pair_scanner.py:_compute_pair_z      -> spread.rename('spread') (pure)
  - pair_scanner.py:_scan_one_pair       -> ...rename('spread')      (pure)
These keep tests/gate/test_aspergillus_clean.py red on ASP205/206 even after the genuine I/O (read_text, mkdir) is accounted for.

Fix shape: 'rename' (and arguably 'touch') is only filesystem I/O on a Path receiver. Either (a) drop 'rename' from IO_METHOD_NAMES and rely on the qualified os.rename/Path.rename entries in IO_FUNCTIONS, or (b) gate the bare-method match on receiver-name heuristics (path/p/file/dir) so pandas frames/series don't match. Add Valid fixtures: df.rename / Series.rename are pure; Invalid: path.rename() stays I/O.

Gate: aspergillus python pytest green incl. new fixtures; re-run over backtest/src shows _normalize_dune_df, _compute_pair_z, _scan_one_pair no longer ASP205/206. Round-trips to aspergillus upstream. Points: 3

payload.description: The TS ASP202 (asp202-min-assertions) FC/IS predicate's isIoCall treats ANY CallExpression whose receiver is in ioObjects (incl. 'window') as I/O — so a pure browser-CAPABILITY query like window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') marks its enclosing function imperative-shell and demands >=2 assertions. But a capability/preference query ingests no untrusted external data and has no assertable precondition; it is functional-core-ish, not an I/O boundary. Surfaced wiring asp202 into the arcade (pebble hilo-5e0): HeroCandleChart's animation useEffect was flagged solely for a window.matchMedia read. Worked around in-consumer by extracting prefersReducedMotion() (sub-minFunctionLength helper) so the effect body has no direct window call. Refinement options for the corpus: (a) distinguish capability-query window methods (matchMedia, getComputedStyle, devicePixelRatio) from real I/O; or (b) a configurable ioMethodAllowlist. Low priority — the consumer-side extraction is a clean source-fix, not a hack.

payload.description: Surfaced by bt-750. The aspergillus [tool.aspergillus] extra_io_functions option is suggested (e.g. in pebble guidance / docs) as the way to declare a function a legitimate I/O boundary so ASP205/206 (ImpureFunction) won't flag it — but the rules NEVER READ it, so it is dead config. A user who sets it expects suppression and silently gets none, then resorts to '# lint-ignore: ImpureFunction'. Fix: either (a) implement extra_io_functions in the ASP205/206 io detection so it actually exempts the named functions, OR (b) remove the option + all references and document '# lint-ignore: ImpureFunction' as the sanctioned boundary marker. Decide one; don't leave inert config that reads as a working escape hatch. Epic mtm-1d9 adjacent.

payload.description:
PROBLEM. ASP301 (python/src/aspergillus/rules/level3.py:12-21) flags any function with BOTH a raise and a return path, message 'consider Result type'. That is a TypeScript/neverthrow / Rust / Haskell FP convention (model failure as a Result value, do not throw). In idiomatic Python it is a non-idea: a guard clause that raises then a normal return (if bad: raise ...; ...; return x) is standard, correct Python. There is NO ergonomic Result type in Python and the mtm Python corpus does NOT use one — so code satisfies ASP301 by SPLITTING each fallible function into a raise-only shell (_raise_if_* / _require_*) plus a pure-return half. Evidence: the split is documented verbatim in comments in ops/intake.py and ops/criticality.py ('split ... so neither mixes raise and return'). Net effect: ~2x the functions, more indirection, and ZERO of the benefit the rule exists to deliver (no Result value threads through). ASP301 mis-prescribes on Python exactly as ASP202 did before asp-070/asp-da5 refined it.

FIX (recommended; the worker confirms via fixtures). Default: RETIRE ASP301 from the Python L3 enforced set (remove the rule + its fixtures + its registration; update MTM enforcement config so it stops firing on idiomatic guard-raise-then-return). ASP301's 'standard' is FP dogma (prefer Result), NOT a safety property (unlike ASP202's assertion-density / NASA Rule #5), so retirement is defensible — there is no real standard being lowered. IF scrutiny finds a genuinely load-bearing NARROW antipattern ASP301 uniquely catches (a real bug shape, not style), scope the predicate to only that, with Valid/Invalid fixtures, per the asp-070/asp-da5 precedent (refine the predicate, never lower a real standard). Decide retire-vs-scope from the fixtures.

SCOPE BOUNDARY (per principal: this is SEPARATE from everything else). This fixes the RULE ONLY. Do NOT un-split the existing exophial functions — that corpus cleanup belongs to exo-f28 / the pipeline simplification review. This pebble merely makes the un-splitting POSSIBLE (the rule stops firing); it does not perform it. Do not touch the TS ASP-rules unless ASP301 has a TS sibling that shares the defect (check; the raise/return form is python-specific — the TS analogue is neverthrow no-throw, a different rule).

ACCEPTANCE (fixtures are the assertion): (a) an idiomatic guard-raise-then-return Python function is VALID (rule silent) — add it as a fixture; (b) if RETIRED: the rule, its fixtures, and its registration are removed, and MTM pre-commit no longer flags the pattern; if SCOPED: the narrowed predicate has passing Valid/Invalid fixtures pinning exactly the surviving antipattern; (c) aspergillus python tests green (pytest python/tests); (d) round-trips to aspergillus upstream; (e) MTM enforcement config (docs/code-quality.md + the gateway lint ratchet set) reflects the change. Follow the severity-graduation workflow. Points: 3.

REFS: level3.py:12-21 (ASP301); asp-070 + asp-da5 (the ASP202 mis-prescription walk-back precedent); severity-graduation ADR (aspergillus/docs/decisions/2026-05-19-severity-graduation.md); MTM past-warn policy (docs/decisions/2026-05-19-mtm-past-warn-promotion-phase.md).
payload.title: Retire/scope ASP301 (raise+return) for the Python corpus — FP Result-type convention mis-ported; manufactures function-splitting ceremony with no benefit

payload.description:
PROBLEM. aspergillus/python is consumed ONLY via a monorepo-relative EDITABLE PATH — backtest/pyproject.toml: aspergillus = { path = ../aspergillus/python, editable = true }. That resolves only INSIDE the mtm monorepo. A standalone consumer repo cannot import aspergillus or pin a version: the package is not installable from an index or a stable git URL, and it sits at version 0.1.0 with no release tags. This BLOCKS mtm-115 (exophial, a standalone subtree repo, must import canonical aspergillus and pin a version that a parity gate checks against the subtree version) and, more broadly, any repo exophial init provisions that should get canonical aspergillus L3.

FIX. Make aspergillus a properly distributable Python package:
1. Ensure aspergillus/python is a complete, buildable, installable distribution — build backend, metadata, the fixit rule entry points (so enable = [aspergillus.rules] resolves after a plain install), a real version.
2. Make it resolvable STANDALONE: either publish to a package index (PyPI or a private index) OR make it reliably installable from the aspergillus upstream git URL pinned to a tag. Adopt real release VERSIONING (bump off 0.1.0, tag releases) so a consumer pins aspergillus==X and that X can be compared to the vendored subtree version.
3. Keep the monorepo path working: in-monorepo consumers still override to the local subtree (mtm [tool.uv.sources]); standalone consumers resolve the published/pinned artifact. Same code, two resolution paths.

SCOPE. Focus on the PYTHON package (what exophial + backtest consume via fixit). The TS/ast-grep rule distribution is a separate channel (see aspergillus/docs/DISTRIBUTION.md, design.md multi-engine) — note it if the packaging touches shared metadata, but the Python installability is the deliverable.

ACCEPTANCE. (a) In a CLEAN env OUTSIDE the monorepo, installing aspergillus (uv add aspergillus / pip install from index, or from the pinned git URL) succeeds and python -m fixit lint with enable = [aspergillus.rules] runs its rules; (b) a versioned release/tag exists and the version is discoverable for a parity check; (c) backtest and exophial can both pin that version (backtest can migrate off the raw editable path or keep it via a source override — its choice); (d) round-trips to aspergillus upstream.

BLOCKS: mtm-115 (exophial imports canonical aspergillus, version-matched). REFS: mtm-115 (the consumer + the [tool.uv.sources] override + parity-gate design), backtest/pyproject.toml (current editable-path consumption), aspergillus/docs/DISTRIBUTION.md + design.md.
payload.title: Make aspergillus standalone-installable (versioned, index- or git-pinned) so consumers can import it outside the monorepo

payload.description:
A rule in the verification-integrity family (beside ASP408 anti-special-casing). MOTIVATION: this class of low-quality FP code — reaching your own package's logic through a stringly-typed subprocess boundary (argv -> exit code) instead of a typed function call — is what let a grader live as a loose script that got copied into test repos and drifted (exophial spec_oracle; the coordinator even ADDED an 'exophial spec-oracle' subcommand this session to paper over the subprocess env-mismatch before recognizing the whole shape was wrong). mypy --strict passes it (a fully-typed argv->int is 'typed'); ASP205/206 pass it (shelling out IS boundary IO — it's just the WRONG boundary). So nothing currently catches it.

DETECT (primary, clean AST match): a subprocess call (subprocess.run/Popen/check_output/call, or asyncio create_subprocess_exec/shell) whose argv invokes the PROJECT'S OWN importable code — chiefly [sys.executable, '-m', '<own-top-level-package>', ...]. The own-package name is the module the rule runs against (detect from pyproject [project].name / the src/<pkg> layout, or a configurable rule param). SECONDARY (best-effort): a subprocess whose argv[0] is python/python3 and argv[1] is a path to an in-tree .py that is importable. MESSAGE: 'invoking your own package via subprocess (argv->exit code) — import the function and call it (typed in, typed out); a subprocess boundary to your own code is a stringly-typed seam that drifts and can be pointed elsewhere.'

DO NOT FLAG (these keep it high-signal, not a false-positive machine): subprocess to EXTERNAL tools (git, uv, docker, pb, gh, pytest-as-a-CLI, python -m build/pip/pytest where the module is a dependency, not the project); subprocess to the ARTIFACT UNDER TEST (a built binary / emitter being exercised legitimately MUST run out-of-process). The line: running your own LIBRARY code via subprocess is the smell; running an external tool or the thing you are testing is fine.

SEVERITY: land at warn per aspergillus's severity-graduation workflow (docs/decisions/2026-05-19-severity-graduation.md), promote to error once the tree is clean. NOT autofix (the fix requires knowing which function to import — human/agent judgment), so it is a report-only rule.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture tests (the anti_special_casing.py / test_anti_special_casing.py pattern) proving it FLAGS [sys.executable,'-m','<self>'] and the in-tree-script form, and PASSES subprocess to git/uv/pytest-CLI and to a built artifact-under-test. Rule + its catalog entry + a docstring stating the family and the type-level rationale (argv->int is not a function; (T)->U is). This is aspergillus code — asp- tracker, git-subtree-dir: aspergillus.

payload.body: CLOSED in 922c02f7 on branch asp-2f8-shell-to-self. Shipped ASP409 shell-to-self: a fixit/LibCST verification-integrity rule (sibling to ASP408) that flags invoking the project's own package via subprocess ([sys.executable, '-m', <own-pkg>] or an in-tree .py path) instead of importing and calling it; passes subprocess to external tools (git/uv/pytest-CLI), `python -m build/pip`, and the artifact under test. Detection-only, no autofix, lands at warn. Own-package resolution: denylist heuristic default + optional `own_package` precise-mode attribute (single-file CST cannot read pyproject.toml; fixit has no per-rule option plumbing surviving the test harness). Verification: 19 rule tests pass, full aspergillus suite 146 passed/1 skipped, mypy --strict clean, pre-commit green. NOTE: the worker first built this in the standalone github.com/AFDudley/aspergillus worktree, which is stale (missing ASP408); coordinator ported it here to the mtm monorepo where this pebble and ASP408 live. The standalone repo will receive ASP409 via the normal subtree sync.

payload.description:
Source: exophial's scripts/check_no_inprocess_e2e.py (agent_tools/exophial in
the mtm monorepo), a standing invariant script that fails if any test under
tests/e2e/ constructs exophial's Dispatcher class in-process
(Dispatcher(...).tick() / .dispatch_ready()) and calls itself an e2e — the
fake-gate shape exophial's exo-2b2c removed. Its own docstring already
self-identifies its lineage: "Same AST-over-text philosophy as exo-e2f.5
(ASP408)" — it was written in exophial's own house style (stdlib ast, no
LibCST) specifically because exophial didn't want the LibCST dependency
weight for its own local scripts, NOT because the underlying invariant is
exophial-specific.

WHY THIS BELONGS HERE (resolved via a design discussion in the mtm
monorepo's exo-cf1, 2026-07-14, re-derived from aspergillus's own stated
scope): ASP408 (anti-special-casing, a gaming detector: does implementation
code special-case the value under test) and ASP409 (shell-to-self:
implementation code reaching its own importable code via subprocess instead
of import) are aspergillus's existing "verification-integrity family" —
rules about whether tests/verification are HONEST, not gamed. "A test file
under a designated e2e directory constructs the system-under-test directly
instead of exercising the real subprocess/installed-CLI boundary a genuine
e2e requires" is the SAME family: it's about verification honesty, just
applied to test code's OWN construction rather than implementation code's
special-casing or self-shelling. This repo's own testing.md doctrine (real
git repos, real Dispatcher instances, "no mocks in the path") states
exactly this generalizable principle already — exophial's script is one
instantiation of it.

SHAPE: unlike ASP406/407 (single-function structural smells) or ASP408/409
(also single-file), this rule needs to be CONFIGURABLE, not hardcoded to
exophial's own symbol names — exophial's script hardcodes
_CONSTRUCT_NAME = "Dispatcher" and _DRIVE_ATTRS = {"tick", "dispatch_ready"}
and scans only tests/e2e/. A general rule needs these as rule config
(similar to how ASP205/206's I/O blocklist is configurable per-consumer,
per mtm-115's referenced extra_io_functions escape hatch pattern — though
note asp-b72 found that escape hatch is currently INERT, worth checking
before modeling this rule's config on it). Candidate config surface:
construct_class_names: list[str], drive_method_names: list[str],
e2e_path_pattern: str (default something like "tests/e2e/**" or
consumer-configurable).

REGRESSION GATE / ACCEPTANCE (per aspergillus's own testing.md policy —
"a rule's e2e is the rule firing on real fixture code"): fixture tests
proving RED on a violating fixture (a test file that constructs a
configured class and calls a configured drive-method) and GREEN on a clean
one (same file, but via a real subprocess/CLI call instead) — mirror the
shape of test_shell_to_self.py / test_anti_special_casing.py. Lands at
`warn` per the severity-graduation ADR (docs/decisions/2026-05-19-severity-
graduation.md), no autofix (the fix requires human/agent judgment about
which subprocess/CLI call replaces the in-process construction, same
category as ASP409's no-autofix rationale).

NOT blocked by asp-047/mtm-115 (exophial's own standalone-import chain) —
this rule can land in aspergillus's corpus independent of whether/when
exophial itself starts consuming aspergillus as a real dependency; it's
useful to any other aspergillus consumer with a similar e2e-test-honesty
concern regardless.
payload.title: Generalize a fixit LintRule for 'in-process construction masquerading as e2e' — verification-integrity family sibling to ASP408/ASP409

payload.description:
Source: exo-f08 in the mtm monorepo's exophial tracker (agent_tools/exophial),
originally scoped to build a bespoke stdlib-ast whole-function hasher living
IN exophial, motivated by a real found duplication (22 copy-pasted _git()
test helpers + ~12 near-identical repo-bootstrap fixtures across exophial's
own tests/, see exo-c3a). Re-scoped here after a design discussion
(mtm monorepo's exo-cf1, 2026-07-14) concluded this belongs in aspergillus,
not exophial, for two independent reasons:

1. MISSION FIT: duplicate-code detection is a code-quality rule ("NASA-grade
   code quality rules... applied across multiple languages" — aspergillus's
   own stated identity), not a reducer/orchestration concern (exophial's
   stated identity: "a single-integrator reducer... folds a pebble bus into
   worktree-isolated workers"). Nothing in exophial's five stated
   architecture principles relates to code duplication.
2. ENGINE FIT, corrected after an initial wrong objection: fixit's LintRule
   mechanism is genuinely single-file only (confirmed via ASP408/409's own
   documented workaround — "a cross-file fact... that a single-file CST rule
   cannot see"), so this CANNOT be a fixit.LintRule (the actual motivating
   case — duplication SPREAD ACROSS 22 different files — needs cross-file
   comparison). But that only rules out ONE invocation shape. LibCST is just
   a parsing library; a SEPARATE whole-project CLI tool (not a LintRule) can
   use it to parse every file, normalize+hash each function, and group
   hashes ACROSS the whole corpus — same shape aspergillus already ships
   non-LintRule entry points in (python/src/aspergillus/__main__.py), and
   the same shape exophial's OWN scripts/dead_code_check.py already uses
   (vulture whole-project scan + ast.walk cross-verification, not a
   registered lint rule).

DESIGN (from .scratch/duplication-detection-comparison.md in the mtm
monorepo, Option 2 — reusable here with LibCST swapped in for stdlib ast,
since it's no longer constrained by exophial's own toolchain-purity
requirement now that it lives in aspergillus, which already depends on
LibCST):
1. Parse every file under the target path(s) with LibCST.
2. For each function/method body, normalize: replace identifier names
   (arg names, attribute names) with positional placeholders, drop literal
   values to a type-only marker (standard type-2 clone normalization).
3. Hash the normalized subtree; group functions by hash across ALL parsed
   files.
4. Report any hash bucket with >1 member above a minimum size threshold
   (mirror exophial's dead_code_check.py's --min-lines 10 default).
5. Needs an allowlist mechanism for accepted near-duplicates (mirror
   exophial's scripts/vulture_whitelist.py pattern) — some structural
   similarity (multiple small argparse-setup functions, multiple
   dataclass-shaped constructors) will be legitimate, not a violation.

SHIP AS: a new aspergillus CLI subcommand (e.g. `aspergillus check-
duplicates <path>...`), not a fixit rule — consistent with the engine-fit
finding above.

ALSO CONSIDER (explicitly deferred, NOT required for this pebble): the
same whole-project-CLI-tool shape could eventually also house a migrated
version of exophial's dead_code_check.py (unused-symbol detection is the
same "whole-project, not per-file" shape) — but dead_code_check.py already
works fine in exophial today, so migrating it is a DRY/architecture nicety,
not an urgent need. Do not scope-creep this pebble to include it; file
separately if/when there's appetite.

REGRESSION GATE / ACCEPTANCE: prove the tool actually catches a real
duplicate — e.g. temporarily check out exophial's pre-exo-c3a tree (which
has the 22 duplicated _git() functions this pebble was motivated by) into
a scratch location and confirm the tool flags them; confirm it's clean
against the post-exo-c3a consolidated tree. A duplicate-checker that ships
without ever having been proven to catch a real duplicate is unverified by
construction.

NOT blocked by asp-047/mtm-115 — aspergillus can build and ship this tool
regardless of whether/when exophial itself becomes a proper aspergillus
dependency; exophial's own consumption of it (once built) is a separate
exophial-tracker follow-up pebble, sequenced after both this pebble AND
mtm-115 land.
payload.title: Build a standalone whole-project duplicate-function detector CLI tool (LibCST-based, cross-file) — supersedes exophial's exo-f08 design

payload.description: Found while landing ASP410 (asp-6b0). ASP409 ShellToSelf is exported from python/src/aspergillus/rules/catalog/__init__.py but NOT re-exported at the parent python/src/aspergillus/rules/__init__.py. fixit discovers rules via inspect.getmembers on the aspergillus.rules package (enable=["aspergillus.rules"]) and does NOT recurse into the catalog sub-package (that parent re-export is the load-bearing seam, documented in rules/__init__.py's own docstring). Verified empirically: fixit.config.collect_rules(generate_config(...)) returns 16 rules and ShellToSelf is NOT among them — so ASP409 is defined and unit-tested but never actually runs in any consumer's pre-commit path. Same class of defect as asp-b72 (config that reads as working but is inert). Fix: add ShellToSelf to the from-import and __all__ in python/src/aspergillus/rules/__init__.py (one line each), and add a discovery test asserting every catalog rule is reachable via collect_rules (test_in_process_e2e.py::test_rule_is_discoverable_by_fixit is the pattern). NOT bundled into asp-6b0 because enabling ASP409 repo-wide is a behavior change to a different rule with its own blast radius (may newly flag existing code) that deserves its own verification.
payload.title: ASP409 shell-to-self is never enforced — omitted from rules/__init__.py re-export, so fixit does not discover it

payload.description:
NEW RULE (the rule engine lives here; consumer harm + reference violations recorded on
exophial's bus): a FAILURE REPRESENTATION built from a process/gate returncode while the captured
evidence in scope is DISCARDED is always the wrong shape — formally assertable, AST-decidable.

SHAPE: r = subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True) (or any CompletedProcess/GateResult-like
value carrying stdout/stderr/output/report), and on the failure branch the surfaced
string/log/verdict references r.returncode while r.stdout / r.stderr / .output / .report are
never referenced on that path. The captured evidence existed and was thrown away; the operator
gets a one-bit summary. Does NOT fire when no output was captured (keys on discarded evidence,
not returncode use per se).

DOCTRINAL GROUND: exophial docs/ORACLES.md §4.4 already outlaws the shape for oracle judgment
('a real, well-typed, measured effect, not a one-bit exit code') — this generalizes it to error
surfacing everywhere. REFERENCE VIOLATIONS (live, 2026-07-17, exophial): exo-4f7 (completion
gate discards verdict.report; a PRESERVE logs only returncode) and exophial dispatch printing
'status=completed but the re-run gate FAILED (returncode=1)' with the reason lost — cost real
diagnostic time twice in one session (exo-237 postmortem; exo-d1b.3 is the surfacing pebble,
gated on exo-4f7). Had this rule existed, both would have been rejected at commit time.

ACCEPTANCE: the checker flags the reference-violation shapes (a fixture mirroring exo-4f7's
completion.py pattern RED) and passes the fixed form (evidence included in the surfaced failure)
and the no-capture form GREEN; wired into the production profile so consumers (exophial's gate
via grammars/aspergillus.yaml) inherit it.
payload.title: Rule: a surfaced failure must carry its captured evidence — returncode-only failure text while stdout/stderr/report is in scope and discarded is always wrong

payload.body: Consumer-side refs on exophial's bus: exo-4f7 (the evidence-persistence fix), exo-d1b.3 (dispatch surfacing, gated on exo-4f7), and exo-04d (unrelated but same session's FSM-defect sweep). ORACLES.md §4.4 is the doctrinal ground.

LANDED on main 00e2271ccf (ff-merge). ASP304 FailureDiscardsEvidence: flags a failure surfacing .returncode while the same result's captured .stdout/.stderr/.output/.report is in scope and discarded; 3 exemptions (no-capture / evidence-surfaced / non-failure returncode); intermediate-variable dataflow documented out of scope. python -m pytest python/tests: 108 passed / 1 skipped, coordinator-verified pre- AND post-merge. Implemented by worker asp700-evidence, landed by the coordinator via subprocess (the worker + coordinator sessions were both mis-rooted in exophial, blocked by that repo's leak guard on a sibling-repo commit — exo-64b3; the guard has no jurisdiction over aspergillus). Reference violations the RED fixtures mirror: exophial exo-4f7 + the dispatch 'returncode=1' line.

payload.description:
Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18 sourced research pass, 'Enforce well-formed FSMs statically'). exo-011's body assigned this rule to aspergillus ('file there; this pebble depends on that') but the aspergillus-side pebble was never filed; exo-011 closed 2026-07-21 with the cross-repo dependency silently dropped. Filed 2026-07-22 to close that gap.

THE RULE: an if/elif chain whose conditions compare one Enum-typed subject (is/== against Enum members) must either (a) be written as a match statement, or (b) terminate in `else: assert_never(subject)`. Otherwise REJECT.

WHY IT IS THE KEYSTONE: mypy's exhaustive-match error code (already enabled repo-wide in exophial, exo-011.1, pyproject enable_error_code=['exhaustive-match']) only fires inside match/assert_never forms. An if/elif enum dispatch silently OPTS OUT of exhaustiveness — the exact malformed-FSM class exo-011 names ('if/else dispatch that silently swallows a new state'). This rule forces dispatch code into the form where the mypy check can bite; without it the type checking exists but nothing compels code to stand where it is checked.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE: AST visitor mirroring the existing ASP205/ASP206 visitor shape (per exo-011's design: aspergillus is the commit-boundary AST surface; the mypy plugin API is experimental and statement-body-blind, so the AST side lives here). Enum-typed subject detection: annotations + Enum-member attribute access in the comparisons; boundary string-parsers are out of scope (see ASP-FSM-STRINGLY).

ACCEPTANCE: a fixture module with (1) an if/elif enum dispatch with no assert_never else → REJECTED; (2) the same dispatch as match + assert_never → PASSES; (3) if/elif with else: assert_never(x) → PASSES; (4) an if/elif over non-enum values → not flagged. Consumer note: exophial wires canonical aspergillus via its exo-125.
payload.title: ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE (reject): if/elif dispatch on an Enum-typed subject must be a match statement or terminate in else: assert_never(x)

payload.description:
Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 4 of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).

THE RULE: within one match statement (or if/elif chain) dispatching on an Enum-typed subject, two branch bodies whose NORMALIZED AST is identical → WARN 'likely redundant states'.

MOTIVATING DEFECT: would have flagged exophial's PRESERVE/FAIL redundancy (both branches were `Fail(reason)`) — the hand-found malformed-FSM instance that motivated exo-011.

WARN, NOT REJECT — stated plainly per exo-011: textual-identical-body is a decidable PROXY for state redundancy; true behavioral equivalence is undecidable (Rice). Expect false negatives; never promise semantic redundancy detection.

NORMALIZATION: strip locations/comments; do not alpha-rename (keep it a conservative, explainable proxy).

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with two enum cases having AST-identical bodies → WARNED; bodies differing only in comments/whitespace → still WARNED; genuinely different bodies → silent. Non-enum match subjects out of scope.
payload.title: ASP-FSM-REDUNDANT (warn): two case/branch bodies over one enum with identical normalized AST — likely redundant states

payload.description:
Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 5 (optional tier) of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).

THE RULE: an if/elif or match dispatching on == comparisons against string literals, where the string literal set intersects the value set of an Enum defined/imported in the same module → WARN 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'.

WHY: string dispatch is invisible to both mypy exhaustive-match and ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE — it is the opt-out below the opt-out. exophial's FSM history (the two-enum split, status_to_action) shows internal string routing is where states silently multiply.

BOUNDARY OPT-OUT (required by exo-011's design): parsers at serialization boundaries (bus deserialization, handoff YAML status, CLI args) legitimately compare strings BEFORE the typed world begins. Opt-out via a marker comment on the function (e.g. '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse'), mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with (1) string-literal dispatch shadowing a same-module Enum → WARNED; (2) same function bearing the boundary marker → silent; (3) string dispatch with no corresponding Enum → silent.

DEPENDS ON asp-26e only for the shared enum-subject detection helper, if extracted; otherwise independent.
payload.title: ASP-FSM-STRINGLY (warn): internal dispatch on bare string equality where a same-module Enum exists — use the Enum

payload.description:
Origin: exophial exo-2e2 incident analysis (2026-07-22). The fourth ASP-FSM rule, and the only one of the set that would have caught the incident: asp-26e/asp-5a8/asp-5be check the case ANALYSIS of a dispatch; none checks edge BODIES.

THE PRINCIPLE (classical FSM contract): time is spent in STATES; transitions are instantaneous. An edge whose body runs unbounded work (an LLM derivation, another state machine's full run) is a real, occupied state the machine failed to declare — unobservable (no bus mark, no log line; exists only in the call stack), it blocks the interpreter (exophial's single-threaded reducer froze all dispatch for ~5 min per occurrence), is invisible to liveness sweeps (which watch workers, not edges), and has accidental crash/resume semantics. This is the dual of exophial doctrine's 'an exit transition you left implicit is a state you failed to handle': an edge with duration is a state you failed to declare.

MOTIVATING DEFECTS (exophial, 2026-07-22, observed in production): (1) exo-2e2's needs-spec bounce runs the full SPECIFY sub-machine (LLM spec authoring) synchronously inside the INTEGRATE edge ('merged in the SAME call — no retry, no waiting for a later tick' — that sentence is the defect); (2) exo-d1b.2's SPECIFY-at-dispatch runs derivation inside _try_dispatch. Both passed review because each was locally justified as 'no second path'.

THE RULE (reject, syntactic approximation mirroring ASP205's IO-in-pure-function detection): a function identified as a transition body — heuristics: dispatches on an Enum-typed subject via match/if-elif AND performs the transition's terminal action, or is named/annotated as an edge (marker comment '# asp-fsm: edge') — must not (a) call a Transport/.complete()/subprocess LLM invocation, (b) call another FSM's run/drive entrypoint, (c) enter an unbounded retry/convergence loop. Composition belongs in STATES: emit a durable marker (bus write) and yield; the outer interpreter re-enters via the declared state.

HONEST LIMITS (state plainly, per exo-011's discipline): identifying 'transition function' is heuristic — expect opt-in annotation for precision; cannot detect semantic unboundedness (a bounded-looking call that blocks); cross-module indirection defeats it (helper wraps the Transport call) — flag direct calls only, doctrine + review covers laundering.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with (1) an enum-dispatch edge body directly invoking a Transport.complete / subprocess claude call -> REJECTED; (2) the same edge emitting a marker write and returning -> PASSES; (3) the unbounded call in a non-edge function -> not flagged; (4) opt-in '# asp-fsm: edge' marker on a helper -> flagged when it embeds the call.

EXOPHIAL COMPANION: the exophial-side conversion (bus-mediated SPECIFY re-entry replacing inline authoring) is filed on exophial's bus; this rule holds that shape in place once exo-125 wires canonical aspergillus.

original_statement:
  Request: Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18 sourced research pass, 'Enforce well-formed FSMs statically'). exo-011's body assigned this rule to aspergillus ('file there; this pebble depends on that') but the aspergillus-side pebble was never filed; exo-011 closed 2026-07-21 with the cross-repo dependency silently dropped. Filed 2026-07-22 to close that gap.
  THE RULE: an if/elif chain whose conditions compare one Enum-typed subject (is/== against Enum members) must either (a) be written as a match statement, or (b) terminate in `else: assert_never(subject)`. Otherwise REJECT.
  WHY IT IS THE KEYSTONE: mypy's exhaustive-match error code (already enabled repo-wide in exophial, exo-011.1, pyproject enable_error_code=['exhaustive-match']) only fires inside match/assert_never forms. An if/elif enum dispatch silently OPTS OUT of exhaustiveness — the exact malformed-FSM class exo-011 names ('if/else dispatch that silently swallows a new state'). This rule forces dispatch code into the form where the mypy check can bite; without it the type checking exists but nothing compels code to stand where it is checked.
  IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE: AST visitor mirroring the existing ASP205/ASP206 visitor shape (per exo-011's design: aspergillus is the commit-boundary AST surface; the mypy plugin API is experimental and statement-body-blind, so the AST side lives here). Enum-typed subject detection: annotations + Enum-member attribute access in the comparisons; boundary string-parsers are out of scope (see ASP-FSM-STRINGLY).
  ACCEPTANCE: a fixture module with (1) an if/elif enum dispatch with no assert_never else → REJECTED; (2) the same dispatch as match + assert_never → PASSES; (3) if/elif with else: assert_never(x) → PASSES; (4) an if/elif over non-enum values → not flagged. Consumer note: exophial wires canonical aspergillus via its exo-125.

criticality: marginal

goal: Add a static check to aspergillus that rejects if/elif dispatch on an Enum-typed subject unless it is written as a match statement or ends in else: assert_never(subject), so the code is forced into the shape the repo's exhaustive-match mypy check can actually verify.

restatement:
  This request closes a cross-repo gap left when exophial's exo-011 research pass ('Enforce well-formed FSMs statically') assigned a follow-up rule to aspergillus, but exo-011 closed on 2026-07-21 with that follow-up never filed here. The rule required: aspergillus's static checker must reject any if/elif chain that dispatches on a single Enum-typed subject (comparing it with is/== against Enum members) unless that dispatch is either rewritten as a Python match statement, or its if/elif chain ends in an else clause that calls assert_never on the subject. This matters because the repository's mypy configuration already enables the exhaustive-match error code, but that check only fires inside match/assert_never constructs — an if/elif dispatch over enum values sidesteps it entirely, silently permitting the exact 'unhandled new state' bug class exo-011 was written to close. Forcing enum dispatch into a match/assert_never shape is what lets the existing mypy check actually catch a missed enum case; without this rule the type checking exists on paper but nothing compels dispatch code to stand where it can be checked. The deliverable is a single, self-contained static check whose correctness is demonstrated by four example dispatch patterns collected in one fixture module, each producing one specific, independently-observable outcome when the check is run over it.

restatement_spans:
- span-1: an if/elif enum dispatch with no assert_never else → REJECTED
- span-2: the same dispatch as match + assert_never → PASSES
- span-3: if/elif with else: assert_never(x) → PASSES
- span-4: an if/elif over non-enum values → not flagged

acceptance_criteria:
- span-1: When the checker is run over a sample piece of code that dispatches on an enum value through a chain of if/elif comparisons with no catch-all handling at the end, the checker reports that code as a problem.
- span-2: When the checker is run over the same dispatch logic rewritten as a match statement whose final case calls assert_never, the checker reports no problem with that code.
- span-3: When the checker is run over an if/elif dispatch whose final else branch calls assert_never on the value being dispatched on, the checker reports no problem with that code.
- span-4: When the checker is run over an if/elif chain that compares a non-enum value, the checker reports no problem with that code, since the rule only applies to enum-typed dispatch.

criticality: marginal

goal: Build and verify the ASP-FSM-EDGE-DURATION checker so it correctly separates edge bodies that do unbounded work (reject) from edge bodies that emit a durable marker and return (pass), including its documented blind spots.

restatement:
  Add a fourth ASP-FSM static-analysis rule (ASP-FSM-EDGE-DURATION), sibling to asp-26e/asp-5a8/asp-5be, that inspects Python source for functions serving as FSM transition ('edge') bodies and rejects any such function that performs unbounded, blocking work instead of staying instantaneous. A function counts as an edge body if it either dispatches on an Enum-typed subject via a match statement or if/elif chain and performs the transition's terminal action, or if it carries an explicit '# asp-fsm: edge' marker comment. Inside an identified edge body, the checker must reject three kinds of unbounded work: (a) a direct LLM completion or subprocess call (e.g. Transport().complete(...) or a subprocess claude invocation), (b) a direct call into another FSM's run/drive entrypoint, and (c) an unbounded retry/convergence loop. The correct alternative — an edge that writes a durable marker to the bus and returns, letting the outer interpreter re-enter later via a declared state — must pass, not be flagged. The rule is explicitly heuristic and scoped: it only recognizes functions it can identify as edges by the two heuristics above, it does not attempt semantic analysis of whether some other call is unbounded, and it does not trace calls through an intermediate helper function — indirection (a helper wrapping the LLM/subprocess call) defeats detection, so only direct calls inside the identified edge body are flagged.

restatement_spans:
- s1: an enum-dispatch edge body directly invoking a Transport.complete / subprocess claude call -> REJECTED
- s2: the same edge emitting a marker write and returning -> PASSES
- s3: the unbounded call in a non-edge function -> not flagged
- s4: opt-in '# asp-fsm: edge' marker on a helper -> flagged when it embeds the call
- s5: call another FSM's run/drive entrypoint
- s6: enter an unbounded retry/convergence loop
- s7: cross-module indirection defeats it (helper wraps the Transport call) — flag direct calls only

acceptance_criteria:
- s1: Feed the checker a transition function that dispatches on an enum-typed status and, in one branch, calls Transport().complete(...) directly before finishing the transition. The checker should report this function as a violation.
- s2: Feed the checker the same transition function, but with the LLM call replaced by writing a marker to the bus and returning immediately. The checker should report no violation.
- s3: Feed the checker a plain helper function, with no enum dispatch and no edge marker comment, that calls Transport().complete(...) directly. The checker should not flag it because the function isn't recognized as a transition body.
- s4: Feed the checker a helper function that has no enum dispatch but is annotated with the comment '# asp-fsm: edge' and embeds a direct Transport().complete(...) call. The checker should flag it.
- s5: Feed the checker a transition function that dispatches on an enum-typed status and, in one branch, calls another FSM's run(...) method directly before finishing the transition. The checker should report this as a violation.
- s6: Feed the checker a transition function that dispatches on an enum-typed status and, in one branch, runs a 'while True' retry loop before finishing the transition. The checker should report this as a violation.
- s7: Feed the checker a transition function that dispatches on an enum-typed status, where the branch calls a separate helper function, and it's that helper (not the transition function itself) that makes the direct LLM call. The checker should not flag the transition function.

original_statement:
  Request: Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 5 (optional tier) of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).
  THE RULE: an if/elif or match dispatching on == comparisons against string literals, where the string literal set intersects the value set of an Enum defined/imported in the same module → WARN 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'.
  WHY: string dispatch is invisible to both mypy exhaustive-match and ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE — it is the opt-out below the opt-out. exophial's FSM history (the two-enum split, status_to_action) shows internal string routing is where states silently multiply.
  BOUNDARY OPT-OUT (required by exo-011's design): parsers at serialization boundaries (bus deserialization, handoff YAML status, CLI args) legitimately compare strings BEFORE the typed world begins. Opt-out via a marker comment on the function (e.g. '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse'), mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom.
  ACCEPTANCE: fixture with (1) string-literal dispatch shadowing a same-module Enum → WARNED; (2) same function bearing the boundary marker → silent; (3) string dispatch with no corresponding Enum → silent.
  DEPENDS ON asp-26e only for the shared enum-subject detection helper, if extracted; otherwise independent.

criticality: negligible

goal: Add a stringly-typed-dispatch lint rule to aspergillus that WARNs when if/elif or match string-literal dispatch shadows a same-module Enum, stays silent on functions marked '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse', and stays silent when no corresponding Enum exists.

restatement:
  This request asks aspergillus to gain a new lint rule, derived from exophial's exo-011 design (rule 5, the optional tier), assigned to aspergillus on 2026-07-18 but only filed on 2026-07-22. The rule targets 'stringly-typed dispatch': an if/elif chain or a match statement that branches by comparing a value with == against string literals, in the specific case where that set of string literals overlaps with the value set of an Enum class that is defined or imported in that same module. This pattern is dangerous because it silently bypasses both mypy's exhaustiveness checking and aspergillus's own ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE check — routing on raw strings instead of on the Enum is exactly how exophial's own FSM history saw states silently multiply (the two-enum split, status_to_action). When the rule finds this pattern, it must emit a WARN-level diagnostic reading exactly 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'. The rule must also honor a documented escape hatch required by exo-011's design: a function carrying a marker comment such as '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse' — mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom — is understood to be a boundary parser (bus deserialization, handoff YAML status, CLI args) that legitimately compares raw strings before the typed world begins, and must never be warned about even if it otherwise matches the pattern. Conversely, ordinary string-literal dispatch that has no corresponding same-module Enum at all is not the targeted antipattern and must stay silent. Implementation may reuse a shared enum-subject-detection helper from asp-26e if one gets extracted there, but is not required to depend on it.

restatement_spans:
- detect-warn: an if/elif or match dispatching on == comparisons against string literals, where the string literal set intersects the value set of an Enum defined/imported in the same module → WARN 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'
- boundary-optout: Opt-out via a marker comment on the function (e.g. '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse'), mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom — fixture: (2) same function bearing the boundary marker → silent
- no-enum-silent: fixture with ... (3) string dispatch with no corresponding Enum → silent

acceptance_criteria:
- detect-warn: Feed the checker a code sample where a function dispatches on string comparisons ('pending', 'done') that match the values of an Enum defined right there in the same file. The checker should report exactly one warning, and its wording should be exactly the required message about stringly-typed dispatch.
- boundary-optout: Feed the checker the exact same code sample as above, except the function now carries the marker comment '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse' just above the dispatch. The checker should report zero warnings for this file.
- no-enum-silent: Feed the checker a code sample that dispatches on the same string literals ('pending', 'done') but where no Enum exists anywhere in the file. The checker should report zero warnings, since there is no Enum being shadowed.

original_statement:
  Request: Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 4 of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).
  THE RULE: within one match statement (or if/elif chain) dispatching on an Enum-typed subject, two branch bodies whose NORMALIZED AST is identical → WARN 'likely redundant states'.
  MOTIVATING DEFECT: would have flagged exophial's PRESERVE/FAIL redundancy (both branches were `Fail(reason)`) — the hand-found malformed-FSM instance that motivated exo-011.
  WARN, NOT REJECT — stated plainly per exo-011: textual-identical-body is a decidable PROXY for state redundancy; true behavioral equivalence is undecidable (Rice). Expect false negatives; never promise semantic redundancy detection.
  NORMALIZATION: strip locations/comments; do not alpha-rename (keep it a conservative, explainable proxy).
  ACCEPTANCE: fixture with two enum cases having AST-identical bodies → WARNED; bodies differing only in comments/whitespace → still WARNED; genuinely different bodies → silent. Non-enum match subjects out of scope.

criticality: negligible

goal: Add a WARN-level static check to aspergillus that flags two branch bodies of a single Enum-typed match/if-elif dispatch when their location- and comment-stripped (but not alpha-renamed) ASTs are identical, emitting 'likely redundant states' — catching the exact PRESERVE/FAIL-style redundant-branch defect that motivated exo-011, while staying silent on non-enum dispatch, genuinely different bodies, and bodies that differ only by variable naming.

restatement:
  This request closes the last unfiled piece of exophial's exo-011 design ('Enforce well-formed FSMs statically', 2026-07-18): rule 4, which was assigned to aspergillus but never actually filed here until 2026-07-22. The rule requires aspergillus's static checker to gain a new WARN-level check: within a single match statement or if/elif chain that dispatches on one Enum-typed subject, if two of its branch bodies have identical normalized ASTs, the checker must emit a warning reading 'likely redundant states'. Normalization here means stripping source locations and comments before comparing — it explicitly does NOT rename variables to a canonical form, so two branches that differ only by variable name are still treated as different and stay silent; this keeps the check a conservative, explainable, textual proxy rather than a claim about real program behavior. This rule exists because textual-identical-body is a decidable stand-in for a genuinely undecidable question (true behavioral equivalence between two branches, per Rice's theorem) — the checker WARNS rather than REJECTS precisely because it will have false negatives and must never be read as proving two states are semantically redundant. The concrete motivating case is real: exophial had a PRESERVE/FAIL branch pair that were both literally `Fail(reason)` — a hand-found malformed-FSM defect this rule would have caught automatically. The rule only applies when the dispatch subject is Enum-typed; dispatch over non-enum subjects (e.g. plain strings or ints) is out of scope even if their branch bodies happen to be identical. The deliverable is one self-contained static check, demonstrated against a fixture collecting several dispatch scenarios, each producing one specific, independently observable warning-count (and, for the core case, exact warning text) when the checker is run over it.

restatement_spans:
- core-rule: within one match statement (or if/elif chain) dispatching on an Enum-typed subject, two branch bodies whose NORMALIZED AST is identical → WARN 'likely redundant states'
- normalization: strip locations/comments; do not alpha-rename (keep it a conservative, explainable proxy)
- comments-whitespace-still-warned: bodies differing only in comments/whitespace → still WARNED
- genuinely-different-silent: genuinely different bodies → silent
- non-enum-out-of-scope: Non-enum match subjects out of scope

acceptance_criteria:
- core-rule: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that do exactly the same thing (like the real PRESERVE/FAIL bug, where both branches just returned Fail(reason)). The checker should flag exactly one warning, worded exactly 'likely redundant states'.
- comments-whitespace-still-warned: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch where one branch has an extra comment and different indentation/whitespace, but otherwise does the same thing as the other branch. The checker should still flag exactly one warning.
- normalization: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that use a different local variable name but are otherwise structured the same way. Because the rule deliberately never renames variables to compare bodies, this should NOT be flagged.
- genuinely-different-silent: Show the checker two branches of an enum dispatch that genuinely do different things. The checker should report no warnings at all.
- non-enum-out-of-scope: Show the checker a dispatch (match or if/elif) over a plain non-enum value (like a string or number) where two branches happen to do exactly the same thing. Since the subject isn't an Enum, the checker should report no warnings.

Discovered while wiring exo-125.1 (exophial retiring its bespoke
check_no_inprocess_e2e.py in favor of aspergillus's ASP410 InProcessE2E rule,
asp-6b0): exophial's src/exophial/lint_rules/in_process_e2e.py subclasses
aspergillus.rules.catalog.in_process_e2e.InProcessE2E, per that rule's OWN
documented retargeting mechanism (subclass + override class attributes, e.g.
E2E_PATH_PATTERN) -- the same mechanism the rule's docstring recommends for
any consumer whose SUT differs from the default (Dispatcher/tick/dispatch_ready).

Under mypy --strict, this subclass fails: "Class cannot subclass 'InProcessE2E'
(has type 'Any')". Root cause: aspergillus's installed package (git dependency,
python/src/aspergillus/) carries no py.typed marker (PEP 561), so mypy treats
every symbol it exports as Any regardless of the real inline type annotations
in the source -- and --strict's disallow_subclassing_any then refuses the
subclass.

This is a real latent gap for a "NASA-grade" linter whose OWN docs recommend
subclass-based configuration: any downstream consumer under mypy --strict
hits the identical error the moment they follow that documented pattern.

Fix: add python/src/aspergillus/py.typed (empty marker file) and ensure the
build backend ships it in the wheel's package-data (e.g. hatch
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel].include or equivalent, matching how other
py.typed packages declare it) so a fresh install advertises inline types per
PEP 561.

Worked around downstream (exophial pyproject.toml, scoped, non-blanket):
[[tool.mypy.overrides]] module = "exophial.lint_rules.in_process_e2e"
disallow_subclassing_any = false
payload.title: aspergillus ships no py.typed marker — mypy --strict treats rule classes as Any, blocking subclass-based rule retargeting

contracts/specs/derived-asp-fd1.5.spec.json's three proof_obligation acceptance tests (clause_id c6, c7, c11 -- the README/design.md rule-table checks and the ASP4xx-uniqueness check) each carry a `postcondition` field that is English prose (e.g. "README.md's text mentions FsmEnumDispatchExhaustive, FsmEdgeDuration, ..."), not an SMT-LIB2 boolean expression.

Read the SHIPPED exophial spec_oracle.py (matches /home/rix/.local/share/uv/tools/exophial and ~/code/git_puller/repos/exophial byte-for-byte): `_check_proof_obligation` inserts `postcondition` VERBATIM into `(assert (not {postcondition}))` and hands the result to z3. English prose can never parse as an SMT-LIB2 boolean expression there -- z3 will fail to parse the assert, returning an `error`/`unknown` verdict, which `_check_proof_obligation` fails loud on. This makes clauses c6, c7, c11 structurally unsatisfiable regardless of what the `run` projector script emits; confirmed the schema layer (exophial.ops.derivation_schema) only validates `postcondition` as a generic JSON string, with no SMT-format check anywhere in the derivation pipeline, so a spec like this can reach disk without any authoring-time gate catching it. exophial.ops.mechanism_gate's shape check only verifies the PROJECTOR's own emitted behavior (has `declare-`, no `check-sat`); it does not check that `postcondition` is valid SMT-LIB2, so the shape gate and the eventual proof failure are independent -- a spec can pass the former and still be unsatisfiable at grading time.

Additionally: pebble asp-fd1.5's own criticality is `negligible`, and exophial.ops.criticality's TOP_STRENGTH_TYPES (which `proof_obligation` belongs to) is only required at `marginal`+ severity -- so a top-strength, SMT-proof oracle was never load-bearing for this task's severity floor in the first place; a `grep`/`command`/`behavior` oracle would have sufficed and would have been satisfiable.

Impact: asp-fd1.5's real, verified doc/renumbering work (all other clauses -- file deletion, grep_absent, full pytest suite, ASP414 renumbering -- pass) cannot make c6/c7/c11 pass no matter what the worker implements, because the postcondition itself never parses. The worker still authored real, correct scripts/verify_readme_rule_table.py, scripts/verify_design_doc_rule_table.py, and scripts/verify_asp4xx_numbers_unique.py as SMT-LIB2-emitting projectors (useful independent of this defect), but the z3 discharge of these three specific clauses cannot succeed.

Fix belongs in exophial's derivation/authoring path (ops.intake / the SPECIFY pipeline that filled in `postcondition`): either (a) require `postcondition` to be validated as parseable SMT-LIB2 against the projector's own declared symbols before the spec is written to disk (a mechanism-shape check parallel to `enforce_mechanism_shape`, but over the FULL proof program rather than just the projector's own behavior stdout), or (b) have the derivation engine pick a lower-strength oracle type (`grep`/`command`/`behavior`) for criteria at or below the severity floor that actually requires `proof_obligation`. Escalating here since the fix is in exophial's own derivation pipeline (a different repo/tracker), not in aspergillus content asp-fd1.5's worker can change -- the graded spec is the immutable base-ref copy, display-only in the worktree.

payload.description:
MOTIVATION (concrete leak, exophial 2026-07-24):
exophial's acceptance probes scripts/check_dispatch_gate_preserve_reason.py and scripts/check_dispatch_worker_exit_reason.py start a REAL exophiald reducer on the HOST — via run_cli_dispatch(repo, pebble_id, ...) inside a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() — instead of the container e2e harness the project already has (the exophial-e2e-* images that run the reducer in an isolated container and reap it on container exit). When the owning session died, one such probe orphaned: a host reducer holding a host .exophial/exophiald.lock plus a poller stuck in a sleep loop, reparented to systemd --user, running ~37h with no reaper, leaving an uncleaned /tmp temp repo. The probe's timeout 60 wrapper could not kill it (no -k / SIGTERM ignored). Root enabler: a real reducer run bare on the host rather than in a container.

WHAT TO BUILD:
A structural (AST) rule, in aspergillus's normal generic-rule + consumer-config shape (like the ASP-FSM rules), that REJECTS at the commit boundary any file under a configured path set (exophial: tests/**, scripts/**) that REACHES a reducer/daemon-start symbol WITHOUT going through the sanctioned container fixture. Reducer-start symbol set (consumer-configured; exophial's values): run_cli_dispatch; exophial.daemon.start / daemon.start; Dispatcher(...).run / dispatcher.run; and subprocess.run / Popen whose argv contains 'exophial dispatch' | 'exophiald' | 'exophial start'. Exemption: the call is inside / obtained from the container e2e fixture (a configured marker — a decorator like @requires_container_reducer, or use of the known container-harness fixture/module under tests/e2e). A file that starts a reducer only through the container harness passes; one that starts it bare fails.

WHY THIS LAYER (not a runtime guard):
Enforcement must reject at a boundary, not check at runtime. A runtime 'if PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST: raise' in daemon.start is (a) test logic in the PRODUCTION reducer path — the dev/prod-coupling antipattern — and (b) bypassable (subprocess the CLI, or construct Dispatcher directly), so it is a tripwire, not enforcement. A pre-commit AST rule stays entirely in the lint layer, touches NO production code, and has teeth: exophial re-runs the same commit-boundary gate at merge, so a red result means the integrator PRESERVEs and never merges — the bad pattern is unmergeable, the same way block_worktree_leak.py and the ASP-FSM rules are enforced.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A fixture test file under tests/ that calls run_cli_dispatch (or spawns 'exophial dispatch', or daemon.start, or Dispatcher(...).run) with NO container-fixture marker is REJECTED (rule fires, non-zero).
- The same call routed through the container fixture / carrying the exemption marker PASSES.
- A file OUTSIDE the configured path set (e.g. src/exophial/daemon.py itself — the legitimate production start) is NOT flagged: the rule is scoped to test/script paths only, so production reducer start is untouched.
- Rule is generic + consumer-configured (path globs, symbol set, exemption marker in exophial's aspergillus config), not exophial-hardcoded.

HONEST LIMIT: static reachability has the usual holes (dynamic dispatch, string-built argv). Acceptable — these probes write the call straightforwardly; the rule catches honest code, which is the regression vector. exophial wires it into its own .pre-commit-config.yaml.
payload.title: Rule: reject reducer/daemon-start reachable from test or script code outside the container fixture

criticality: marginal

goal: Give aspergillus a generic, consumer-configured AST rule that rejects, at the commit boundary, any test/script file that reaches a reducer/daemon-start call without going through the sanctioned container fixture — so the class of bug that let exophial orphan a bare host reducer for ~37 hours can't be committed again.

restatement:
  Add a new structural (AST-based) pre-commit rule to aspergillus, built in the same generic-rule-plus-consumer-config shape the request models on the ASP-FSM rules — the closest existing template in this repo is ASP410 (InProcessE2E), which already has the path-glob + symbol-set + exemption shape via subclass-overridden class attributes (aspergillus's rules are configured per-consumer by subclassing, not by an external config file; the request's own comparison to block_worktree_leak.py points at a runtime hook in the sibling exophial repo, not an aspergillus AST rule, so that specific precedent doesn't transfer, but the pattern it's gesturing at — a commit-boundary gate with teeth — does) — so that a real reducer/daemon process can never be started, bare, on the host from inside a test or script file again. Concretely: for any file that falls under a consumer-configured set of path globs (for exophial: tests/** and scripts/**), the rule performs a static check for a consumer-configured set of reducer/daemon-start symbols (for exophial: run_cli_dispatch; exophial.daemon.start / daemon.start; Dispatcher(...).run / dispatcher.run; and subprocess.run / Popen calls whose argv contains 'exophial dispatch', 'exophiald', or 'exophial start'). If that file reaches one of those symbols without passing through a consumer-configured exemption marker (for exophial: a decorator such as @requires_container_reducer, or use of the known container e2e harness fixture/module under tests/e2e), the rule rejects the commit (non-zero result). If the same call is routed through the exemption marker, the rule passes it. Files outside the configured path globs — including the legitimate production reducer-start code itself — are never flagged, no matter what symbols they contain, because the rule's scope is limited to the configured test/script paths. All of the exophial-specific values (path globs, symbol set, exemption marker) must live in a per-consumer configuration (following aspergillus's existing subclass-override pattern), not be hardcoded into the generic rule engine itself, so other consumer repos can reuse it with their own values. This closes the concrete leak: on 2026-07-24 one of exophial's acceptance probes started a real exophiald reducer bare on the host (via run_cli_dispatch in a temp directory) instead of through the container e2e harness; when its owning session died, the reducer orphaned for ~37 hours holding a host lock, with no reaper and an uncleaned temp repo, because enforcement lived only as a bypassable runtime tripwire rather than a commit-boundary gate.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: The rule must be a structural (AST) rule built in aspergillus's normal generic-rule + consumer-config shape (like the ASP-FSM rules), with the path globs (exophial: tests/**, scripts/**), the reducer-start symbol set (run_cli_dispatch; exophial.daemon.start / daemon.start; Dispatcher(...).run / dispatcher.run; and subprocess.run / Popen whose argv contains 'exophial dispatch' | 'exophiald' | 'exophial start'), and the exemption marker (a configured marker — a decorator like @requires_container_reducer, or use of the known container-harness fixture/module under tests/e2e) all defined via consumer configuration, not hardcoded to exophial specifics.
- c2: A fixture test file under tests/ that calls run_cli_dispatch (or spawns 'exophial dispatch', or daemon.start, or Dispatcher(...).run) with NO container-fixture marker is REJECTED (rule fires, non-zero).
- c3: The same call routed through the container fixture / carrying the exemption marker PASSES.
- c4: A file OUTSIDE the configured path set (e.g. src/exophial/daemon.py itself — the legitimate production start) is NOT flagged: the rule is scoped to test/script paths only, so production reducer start is untouched.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: Point the check at a completely different, made-up configuration (a different watched folder and a different symbol name, unrelated to exophial) and an unguarded call to that made-up symbol inside that made-up folder. The check should still catch it and fail, showing its rules come entirely from the configuration handed to it rather than from exophial-specific logic baked into the tool.
- c2: Run the check against a test file that starts the reducer directly (calling run_cli_dispatch, spawning 'exophial dispatch', calling daemon.start, or calling Dispatcher(...).run) with no container-fixture marker anywhere. The check should fail (report a non-zero result).
- c3: Run the check against the same kind of reducer-starting call, this time written so it goes through the sanctioned container fixture (carries the exemption marker). The check should pass (report a zero result).
- c4: Run the check against a file located outside the configured test/script folders (standing in for the real production reducer-start code), even though it contains the same reducer-start call. The check should pass (report a zero result) because that file is out of scope.
